title: Money later is worth less than money now

cues.text: The next five chapters do the mathematics. Properly, and from the beginning. Nothing beyond square roots, fractions and percentages is used, and everything is built in front of you.
A hundred pounds today, and a hundred pounds in a year. Which would you rather have?
Today, obviously. Because you could put today's hundred to work, and have more than a hundred by next year.
Put a hundred pounds somewhere paying five per cent, and in a year you have a hundred and five.
Run that backwards. A hundred and five pounds a year from now is worth exactly a hundred pounds today.
And that is a division. Divide by one point nought five, and you have turned money later into money now.
discounting. Turning money you get later into what it is worth today.
A factory that earns five pounds a year, for ever. Here is the five pounds, arriving year after year.
But each one has to be discounted back. The five pounds in year one is divided once. Year two, twice. Year three, three times. So the far-off ones shrink almost to nothing.
Add up every one of them, all the way out to for ever, and the total is not infinite. It settles on one number.
And the sum is astonishingly simple. Five pounds, divided by nought point nought five. A hundred pounds.
That is the only piece of machinery you need. The value of a stream that goes on for ever is the yearly amount divided by the rate.
And the rate we divide by is the one from chapter two. The cost of capital. What the money has to earn to be worth using.
Five pounds a year at five per cent is worth a hundred.
The same five pounds, when the rate is only two per cent, is worth two hundred and fifty. Cheaper money makes future income worth more.
And at ten per cent it is worth only fifty. Expensive money makes future income worth less.
Hold on to the middle one. It is going to matter enormously in chapter thirteen.
money later is worth less than money now
discounting turns later money into today's money
a stream for ever = yearly amount ÷ the rate
cheaper money makes future income worth MORE
